title: 1958 AHSME Problem 42
statement: In a circle with center \(O,\) chord \(\overline{AB}\) equals chord \(\overline{AC}.\) Chord \(\overline{AD}\) cuts \(\overline{BC}\) in \(E.\) If \(AC=12\) and \(AE=8,\) then \(AD\) equals:

solutions.text:
Because \(E\) lies on \(BC\) and \(AD,\) triangles \(AEC\) and \(ACD\) share angle \(A.\) Also \(\angle ACE=\angle ACB\) subtends chord \(AB,\) while \(\angle ADC\) subtends chord \(AC.\) Since \(AB=AC,\) these angles are equal. Thus \[ \triangle AEC\sim\triangle ACD. \] Corresponding sides give \[ \frac{AE}{AC}=\frac{AC}{AD}. \] Therefore \(\frac{8}{12}=\frac{12}{AD},\) so \(AD=18.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Angles \(ACE\) and \(ADC\) subtend the equal chords \(AB\) and \(AC\)
